Wilkins Ramp-Down Tool: Mathematical Formulation

USACE – Wilkins Spillway Ramp-Down Team

2026-09-23

1. Purpose and linkage to the app

This document walks through the equations behind the Wilkins Spillway ramp‑down dashboard, using the same math as the Shiny application but in a static, reproducible format. It is intended to:

  • Make the ramp‑down logic transparent to operators, biologists, and reviewers.
  • Provide a reference that can be updated alongside the code when spillway tables or capacity curves change.
  • Allow verification of outputs for specific test scenarios without connecting to live USGS data.

Where the live app pulls real‑time data from USGS Water Data APIs through the dataRetrieval package, this report uses simple example values to illustrate calculations.

2. Core inputs and lookup tables

2.1 Spillway gate step table

The Shiny app encodes Wilkins Spillway operations as discrete “steps” describing which gates are open, and uses a lookup table to relate each step to discharge across a range of tailwater elevations.

gate_keys <- paste0("GATE_", 1:11)

# Read the full 1–177 step table from CSV
gate_schedule_lookup <- readr::read_csv(
  "data/wilkins_spillway_step_table.csv",
  na = c("", "NA")
)

# (Optional) add explicit Step 0 = all closed
gate_schedule_lookup <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(
    STEP      = 0L,
    GATE_1    = 0, GATE_2 = 0, GATE_3 = 0, GATE_4 = 0, GATE_5 = 0,
    GATE_6    = 0, GATE_7 = 0, GATE_8 = 0, GATE_9 = 0, GATE_10 = 0, GATE_11 = 0,
    D_215_230 = 0, D_220_230 = 0, D_225_230 = 0,
    D_230     = 0, D_235   = 0, D_240   = 0, D_244   = 0
  ),
  gate_schedule_lookup
)

dplyr::glimpse(gate_schedule_lookup)

gate_schedule_lookup_gate <- gate_schedule_lookup %>%
  select(STEP, all_of(gate_keys))

gate_schedule_lookup_gate %>%
  kable(
    format  = "html",
    caption = "Wilkins Spillway gate openings (ft) by operational step",
    digits  = 2
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed", "hover"),
    full_width = FALSE,
    position   = "left",
    font_size  = 11
  )

The first table summarizes gate openings for each operational step; entries are fractional gate openings in feet for Gates 1–11. Steps progress from all gates closed (Step 0) through the full 177‑step Wilkins operating schedule, ending with all gates fully open. image.jpg

The second table gives the corresponding spillway discharges for each step across several tailwater elevation bands, which are used in the ramp‑down calculations and in the interpolation routine for 𝑄𝑆(tailwater)QS.

(tailwater). image.jpg

Some cells in the discharge columns are NA, indicating that a discharge was not defined for that particular step–tailwater combination; in the math and app code these NA values are simply ignored, and only the available tailwater bands are used when interpolating spillway discharge. image.

The heatmap above shows the gate schedule used by the ramp‑down tool. Warmer colors indicate larger gate openings. Reading downward, each row corresponds to an operational step; reading across, each column corresponds to a gate. This makes it easy to see which gates are used first, how the pattern ramps up, and which steps rely on only a subset of gates. r-statistics

2.2 Wilkins capacity curve

capacity_curve <- tibble(
  Elevation_ft   = c(243, 244, 245, 246, 247),
  Storage_ac_ft  = c(12771.5, 14946.5, 17294, 19820, 22864.5)
)

capacity_curve
## # A tibble: 5 × 2
##   Elevation_ft Storage_ac_ft
##          <dbl>         <dbl>
## 1          243        12772.
## 2          244        14946.
## 3          245        17294 
## 4          246        19820 
## 5          247        22864.

The capacity curve links pool elevation to storage and is used to determine how much volume is available for ramp‑down before reaching the minimum navigation pool. For a given starting elevation, the dashboard converts to storage using this curve, subtracts the volume required to execute the planned ramp‑down, then converts back to a final elevation. If the requested ecological ramp‑down would consume more than the available storage above the navigation minimum, the operation becomes “navigation‑limited” and the duration is shortened accordingly.

ggplot(capacity_curve,
       aes(x = Elevation_ft, y = Storage_ac_ft)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue4", linewidth = 1.3) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue4", size = 2.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Wilkins pool capacity curve",
    x     = "Pool elevation (ft)",
    y     = "Storage (acre-feet)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

3. Spillway discharge calculation

3.1 Tailwater interpolation

get_step_discharge <- function(step_num, tailwater_ft) {
  if (step_num == 0) return(0)
  row <- gate_schedule_lookup %>% filter(STEP == step_num)
  if (nrow(row) == 0) return(0)

  if (tailwater_ft >= 215 && tailwater_ft <= 230) {
    if (!is.na(row$D_215_230)) return(row$D_215_230)
  }

  d_vals <- c(row$D_230, row$D_235, row$D_240, row$D_244)
  interp_pts <- tibble(
    tw  = c(230, 235, 240, 244),
    dis = d_vals
  ) %>% filter(!is.na(dis))

  if (nrow(interp_pts) < 2) return(0)

  approx_fun <- approxfun(interp_pts$tw, interp_pts$dis, rule = 2)
  approx_fun(tailwater_ft)
}

# Example: Step 10 at tailwater 238 ft
get_step_discharge(10, 238)
## [1] 3226.4

3.2 Recognizing the current step from gate telemetry

calc_q_from_gates <- function(g1, g2, g3, g4, g5, g6, g7, g8, g9, g10, g11, tailwater_ft) {
  observed_gates <- c(g1, g2, g3, g4, g5, g6, g7, g8, g9, g10, g11)
  if (all(is.na(observed_gates) | observed_gates == 0)) {
    return(list(step = 0, discharge = 0, distance = 0))
  }

  gate_cols_used <- gate_keys[-7]

  distances <- gate_schedule_lookup %>%
    filter(STEP > 0) %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(
      distance = sqrt(sum((c_across(all_of(gate_cols_used)) - observed_gates[-7])^2, na.rm = TRUE))
    ) %>%
    ungroup()

  best_match <- distances %>% slice_min(distance, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

  list(
    step      = best_match$STEP,
    discharge = get_step_discharge(best_match$STEP, tailwater_ft),
    distance  = best_match$distance
  )
}

# Example gate pattern (roughly Step 10)
example <- calc_q_from_gates(
  g1 = 0.5, g2 = 0.5, g3 = 0.5, g4 = 0.5, g5 = 0.5, g6 = 0.5,
  g7 = 0.0, g8 = 0.0, g9 = 0.5, g10 = 0.0, g11 = 0.5,
  tailwater_ft = 238
)

4. Live data, trends, and risk flags

calculate_trend <- function(df, val_col) {
  if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0) return(list(current = NA, trend = NA))
  if (!val_col %in% names(df))    return(list(current = NA, trend = NA))

  df <- df %>% arrange(dateTime)
  current_row <- tail(df, 1)
  past_time   <- current_row$dateTime - hours(6)
  past_row    <- df %>% filter(dateTime <= past_time) %>% tail(1)

  current_val <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(current_row[[val_col]]))
  trend_val <- if (nrow(past_row) > 0 && !is.na(past_row[[val_col]])) {
    suppressWarnings(as.numeric(current_row[[val_col]]) - as.numeric(past_row[[val_col]]))
  } else {
    NA
  }

  list(current = current_val, trend = trend_val)
}

get_trend_word <- function(trend_val) {
  if (is.na(trend_val))       return("stable")
  if (trend_val >  0.05)      return("rising")
  if (trend_val < -0.05)      return("falling")
  "stable"
}

5. Nettleton depth prediction

predict_nettleton_depth <- function(flow_fulton_cfs, spillway_cfs) {
  depth <- NETT_INTERCEPT +
    NETT_BETA_FULTON * flow_fulton_cfs +
    NETT_BETA_SPILL  * spillway_cfs
  pmax(0, depth)
}

predict_nettleton_depth(5000, 3000)
## [1] 17.0344
total_depth_drop <- function(spillway_start_cfs) {
  NETT_BETA_SPILL * spillway_start_cfs
}

total_depth_drop(3000)
## [1] 3.393

6. Ramp‑down planning math

compute_ideal_duration <- function(Q_start, max_rate_ft_per_hr) {
  total_drop <- total_depth_drop(Q_start)
  max(1, total_drop / max_rate_ft_per_hr)
}

compute_ideal_duration(Q_start = 3000, max_rate_ft_per_hr = 0.10)
## [1] 33.93
build_step_sequence <- function(S_start, target_steps) {
  num_intervals <- min(S_start, target_steps)
  unique(round(seq(S_start, 0, length.out = num_intervals + 1)))
}

build_step_sequence(14, 4)
## [1] 14 10  7  4  0
compute_ideal_volume_af <- function(S_start, tw_ft, target_steps, T_ideal) {
  step_sequence <- build_step_sequence(S_start, target_steps)
  num_intervals <- length(step_sequence) - 1

  sum_q <- 0
  for (i in 1:num_intervals) {
    sum_q <- sum_q + get_step_discharge(step_sequence[i], tw_ft)
  }

  T_ideal * (sum_q * 3600) / (num_intervals * 43560)
}

compute_ideal_volume_af(
  S_start      = 14,
  tw_ft        = 220,
  target_steps = 4,
  T_ideal      = compute_ideal_duration(3000, 0.10)
)
## [1] 9489.885
storage_from_elev <- function(H_ft) {
  approx(capacity_curve$Elevation_ft, capacity_curve$Storage_ac_ft,
         xout = H_ft, rule = 2)$y
}

elev_from_storage <- function(V_af) {
  approx(capacity_curve$Storage_ac_ft, capacity_curve$Elevation_ft,
         xout = V_af, rule = 2)$y
}

H0    <- 245.0
H_nav <- 244.5

V0    <- storage_from_elev(H0)
Vnav  <- storage_from_elev(H_nav)
Vmax  <- max(0, V0 - Vnav)

c(H0 = H0, H_nav = H_nav, V0 = V0, Vnav = Vnav, Vmax = Vmax)
##       H0    H_nav       V0     Vnav     Vmax 
##   245.00   244.50 17294.00 16120.25  1173.75
apply_nav_constraint <- function(S_start, tw_ft, target_steps,
                                 Q_start, H0, H_nav, max_rate_ft_per_hr) {
  T_ideal <- compute_ideal_duration(Q_start, max_rate_ft_per_hr)
  V_ideal <- compute_ideal_volume_af(S_start, tw_ft, target_steps, T_ideal)

  V0   <- storage_from_elev(H0)
  Vnav <- storage_from_elev(H_nav)
  Vmax <- max(0, V0 - Vnav)

  step_sequence <- build_step_sequence(S_start, target_steps)
  num_intervals <- length(step_sequence) - 1
  sum_q <- 0
  for (i in 1:num_intervals) {
    sum_q <- sum_q + get_step_discharge(step_sequence[i], tw_ft)
  }

  if (V_ideal <= Vmax) {
    T_final <- T_ideal
    V_final <- V_ideal
    nav_limited <- FALSE
  } else {
    V_final <- Vmax
    if (sum_q > 0 && V_final > 0) {
      T_final <- V_final * (num_intervals * 43560) / (sum_q * 3600)
    } else {
      T_final <- 0
    }
    nav_limited <- TRUE
  }

  delta_h    <- total_depth_drop(Q_start)
  rate_final <- if (T_final > 0) delta_h / T_final else NA_real_

  H_final <- elev_from_storage(V0 - V_final)

  list(
    T_ideal     = T_ideal,
    V_ideal     = V_ideal,
    T_final     = T_final,
    V_final     = V_final,
    nav_limited = nav_limited,
    rate_final  = rate_final,
    H_final     = H_final,
    drop_ft     = H0 - H_final
  )
}

plan_example <- apply_nav_constraint(
  S_start            = 14,
  tw_ft              = 220,
  target_steps       = 4,
  Q_start            = 3000,
  H0                 = 245.0,
  H_nav              = 244.5,
  max_rate_ft_per_hr = 0.10
)
plan_example

           size = 3,
           color = "steelblue4") +

    title = "Ramp-down decision space: ecological rate vs duration",
    x     = "Ramp-down duration (hours)",

  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

This plot shows how the average Nettleton depth drop per hour decreases as the ramp‑down duration increases. The dashed red line is the ecological ramp‑rate target; the dotted blue line marks the navigation‑limited duration computed from the capacity curve. Any plan to the left of the blue line would overuse storage (violating navigation), and any plan above the red line would exceed the ecological ramp‑rate limit.

build_ramp_scenarios <- function(S_start, tw_ft, target_steps,
                                 Q_start, T_final_hours,
                                 fulton_flow_eff = 4000) {
  start_time   <- floor_date(Sys.time(), "hour")
  duration_sec <- T_final_hours * 3600

  sudden <- tibble(
    Time      = c(start_time - hours(1), start_time, start_time + seconds(60), start_time + seconds(duration_sec)),
    Discharge = c(Q_start, Q_start, 0, 0),
    STEP      = c(S_start, S_start, 0, 0),
    Scenario  = "Sudden Closure (High Risk)"
  )

  if (S_start == 0 || duration_sec == 0) {
    proposed <- sudden %>%
      mutate(Scenario = "Gradual Ramp-Down (Safe/Best Available)")
  } else {
    step_sequence    <- build_step_sequence(S_start, target_steps)
    num_intervals    <- length(step_sequence) - 1
    time_spacing_sec <- duration_sec / num_intervals

    times <- c(start_time - hours(1))
    flows <- c(Q_start)
    steps <- c(S_start)
    current_t <- start_time

    for (i in seq_along(step_sequence)) {
      current_s <- step_sequence[i]
      current_q <- get_step_discharge(current_s, tw_ft)

      if (i > 1) {
        times <- c(times, current_t - seconds(1))
        flows <- c(flows, flows[length(flows)])
        steps <- c(steps, steps[length(steps)])
      }

      times <- c(times, current_t)
      flows <- c(flows, current_q)
      steps <- c(steps, current_s)
      current_t <- current_t + seconds(time_spacing_sec)
    }

    times <- c(times, current_t)
    flows <- c(flows, 0)
    steps <- c(steps, 0)

    proposed <- tibble(
      Time      = times,
      Discharge = flows,
      STEP      = steps,
      Scenario  = "Gradual Ramp-Down (Safe/Best Available)"
    )
  }

  bind_rows(sudden, proposed) %>%
    mutate(
      Predicted_Nettleton_Depth_ft =
        predict_nettleton_depth(
          flow_fulton_cfs = fulton_flow_eff,
          spillway_cfs    = Discharge
        )
    )
}

scenario_example <- build_ramp_scenarios(
  S_start         = 14,
  tw_ft           = 220,
  target_steps    = 4,
  Q_start         = get_step_discharge(14, 220),
  T_final_hours   = plan_example$T_final,
  fulton_flow_eff = 4000
)

ggplot(scenario_example,
       aes(x = Time, y = Discharge, color = Scenario, linetype = Scenario)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Sudden Closure (High Risk)"              = "red",
    "Gradual Ramp-Down (Safe/Best Available)" = "darkgreen"
  )) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(
    "Sudden Closure (High Risk)"              = "solid",
    "Gradual Ramp-Down (Safe/Best Available)" = "dashed"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "Example spillway ramp‑down: sudden vs gradual",
    x = "Time",
    y = "Spillway Discharge (cfs)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_blank())

scenario_long <- scenario_example %>%
  select(Time, Scenario, Discharge, Predicted_Nettleton_Depth_ft) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(Discharge, Predicted_Nettleton_Depth_ft),
    names_to  = "Quantity",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Quantity = factor(Quantity,
                      levels = c("Discharge", "Predicted_Nettleton_Depth_ft"),
                      labels = c("Spillway discharge (cfs)",
                                 "Modeled Nettleton depth (ft)"))
  )

ggplot(scenario_long,
       aes(x = Time, y = Value, color = Scenario, linetype = Scenario)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.0) +
  facet_wrap(~ Quantity, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Sudden Closure (High Risk)"              = "red",
    "Gradual Ramp-Down (Safe/Best Available)" = "darkgreen"
  )) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "dashed")) +
